newsitem.title: UK: Britain sells HMSO stationers for 54 million stg.
newsitem.headline: Britain sells HMSO stationers for 54 million stg.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it had agreed to sell HMSO to the National Publishing Group (NPG) for 54 million stg.

The government announced on July 31 that it had selected NPG, a consortium headed by investment management group Electra Fleming, as preferred bidder for Her Majesty's Stationery Office, which provides printing, publishing, office supplies and related services to government and parliament.
NPG will raise additional finance of 71 million stg to fund invesment, restructuring and working capital for HMSO, public services minister Roger Freeman said in a statement.
Norwich-based HMSO employs some 2,700 staff and had turnover last year of 355 million stg.
Freeman said the privatisation was an excellent deal for the business, its customers and staff.
Formal completion of the deal is expected before the end of the month following discussions on the transfer of HMSO staff to the new owner.
